column1: # The message table of the syntax layer.
# This file is the single source of truth for the messages this repository ships. It is not a
# translation table: it is the list of message IDs and the canonical English text of each, and it is
# what turns "this module's ids are complete" into a checkable property from outside.
#   id     dotted <domain>.<snake_case>, stable forever, never renumbered, never recycled
#   lang   the language the text is written in; always en, and the text must agree with that
#   text   the template, Go-quoted so tabs, quotes and newlines round-trip exactly
# The table is append-only: a message's number is its position here, and the consumer addresses
# these messages by that number, so inserting a row renumbers every message after it. New messages
# Every ID here is reached through a call site that names it (errfID), never through its text: a
# rephrasing changes the text and leaves the identity alone. There is no English-only back door -
# a template that reaches a user is either an ID in this table or it is not a message.

nesting is deeper than %d levels, the limit of this implementation: split the expression into smaller statements
a named struct requires 'type': type struct { ... } %s;
a named interface requires 'type': type interface { ... } %s;
a library body may only contain fn symbol signatures
program declarations support only main / library (lib)
an anonymous struct has no name to export: pub type struct { ... } Name;
an anonymous interface has no name to export: pub type interface { ... } Name;
pub type supports only struct / interface
pub may only prefix fn or type struct/interface (named types require 'type')
the function keyword is 'fn': write fn main(...) rather than func main(...)
a function must declare its return type: fn %s(...) <return type> { ... }
an anonymous struct cannot take generic parameters (write type struct<T> { ... } Name;)
an anonymous interface cannot take generic parameters (write type interface<T> { ... } Name;)
@ signature must follow a function call
'::' requires an identifier on the left
int literal %d out of 32-bit range (int is 32-bit, like C)
